pages.text: The sky above the school ground was filled with colorful kites dancing in the wind. <name> held his bright red kite, “Whistler,” smiling as it soared higher than ever. But suddenly — snap! — the string broke!
“Oh no! Whistler!” shouted <name>, as his kite drifted over rooftops, tumbling and twirling in the wind. Without thinking twice, he raced after it.

He dashed up the stairs of his apartment building, his shoes thumping like tiny drums. At the top, the wind whooshed past his face, but <name> didn’t stop. He climbed onto the terrace wall, arms stretched wide for balance, eyes locked on the red kite fluttering ahead.
“Come on, <name>! You can do it!” cheered his friend Aarav from below.

<name> leaped over a low pipe, crawled under a clothesline, and ran across the roof tiles. The wind tugged his hair, teasing him as if daring him to keep up. Then—there it was! Whistler had landed on the edge of a neighboring roof, tangled around an antenna.
Carefully, <name> stepped closer, balancing like a tightrope walker. One brave reach… got it! He grinned, holding the kite high as the crowd below clapped and whistled.
Sliding down the stairs, <name> ran back to the festival ground. Together, he and Aarav fixed the string and launched Whistler again. The red kite soared, shining proudly in the golden sunlight.
The boys laughed and cheered, their kites racing side by side — proof that courage, balance, and friendship could make any adventure soar!
